paragraphs: U.S. NEV, Battery & Charging Infrastructure Policy Timeline (2010–2026.04)
Based on government public information. Items marked [needs verification] should be cross-checked with original documents.
tables: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) — EV Tax Credits & Battery Manufacturing Grants
Created federal plug-in EV tax credit (§30D, $2,500–$7,500); $2.4B for advanced battery and EV manufacturing grants; $500M for DOE vehicle technologies program. Signed as Public Law 111-5.
Advanced Technology Vehicles Manufacturing (ATVM) Loan Program
Provides loans to advanced vehicle and component manufacturers to improve fuel economy; Ford, Nissan, Tesla have received loans.
The EV Project — Largest Charging Infrastructure Demonstration
$230M project (DOE-funded $114.8M) led by ECOtality deploying ~15,000 chargers across 18 cities; studied charging behavior.
Goal: make EVs as affordable and convenient as gasoline vehicles by 2022. Key targets: battery cost reduction (to $125/kWh), charging infrastructure, lightweight materials, power electronics.
Requires passenger car average fuel economy to reach ~54.5 mpg by 2025 (effectively ~50 mpg), indirectly boosting EV adoption.
DOE Battery and Energy Storage R&D Program
Supports next-gen battery R&D (Li-ion improvement, solid-state research) through VTO and ABR.
Goal: deploy 1.5M ZEVs in California by 2025, including infrastructure build-out and consumer incentives.
Grants for public charging deployment including Workplace Charging Challenge.
$2,500–$7,500 federal tax credit for qualified EV purchases; begins phase-out for manufacturers after 200,000 cumulative sales.
CA Advanced Clean Cars II (ACC II) Rule Path
First long-term ZEV roadmap proposing increasing ZEV sales share. Updated in 2017.
Announced withdrawal from Paris Climate Accord, affecting clean energy/EV policy direction.
Begins freezing/rolling back Obama-era CAFE standards; final 2020 rule reduces target to ~40 mpg.
Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Infrastructure Program
H2@Scale program supports R&D for hydrogen and fuel cell vehicle infrastructure.
Tesla (mid-2018) and GM (end-2018) reach 200,000 vehicles; federal credit phase-out begins (50% reduction every 6 months).
California, NY, NJ and others sign MOU to collaborate on ZEV deployment targets.
DOE Accelerated EV Charging Infrastructure Deployment
R&D and demonstration of fast charging (including 350kW), supporting public fast-charging networks.
SAFE Vehicles Rule Final — One National Program
Finalized freezing CAFE targets at ~40 mpg equivalent; revoked California's Clean Air Act waiver for self-set standards (CA portion blocked by courts).
Authorizes DOE clean energy R&D including energy storage, carbon capture, advanced nuclear, renewables. Provides legal framework for EV/battery R&D.
Directs 100-day review of critical supply chains including EV batteries, semiconductors, critical minerals. Sets foundation for supply chain policy.
Proposed $174B for EV market: charging infrastructure, consumer rebates, school bus electrification, battery manufacturing supply chain.
EO 14037: Strengthening American Leadership in Clean Cars
Sets 50% ZEV target for new car sales by 2030; directs EPA and DOT to revise GHG standards for 2027-2032.
$7.5B for EV charging ($5B NEVI formula, $2.5B competitive grants); $65B for clean energy transmission/grid; electric bus funding. Signed as Public Law 117-58.
DOE 100-Day Supply Chain Assessment: Battery Materials
Published in response to EO 14017, identifying EV battery supply chain vulnerabilities (China dominance), recommending domestic processing capacity.
Implements IIJA NEVI program; states can apply for funding to build EV chargers along interstate highways; interoperability standards required.
DOE Announces $3.16B Battery Manufacturing Funding Opportunity (BIL)
Under BIL, announced $3.16B for domestic battery materials processing and manufacturing facilities — the largest dedicated battery manufacturing grant under BIL framework.
$52.7B for semiconductor manufacturing plus $24B in tax credits. CHIPS for America program (NIST-administered); funds battery and clean energy technology R&D. Public Law 117-167.
Largest clean energy and climate investment ($~370B). Signed as Public Law 117-169 (H.R.5376).

Post-2023: Removes 200k manufacturer cap; adds income limits ($150k single/$225k HOH/$300k joint); MSRP caps ($55k car/$80k SUV/truck); N. America assembly required; battery component and critical mineral sourcing requirements. Credit: up to $7,500 (split $3,750 critical minerals + $3,750 battery components).
First-time used clean vehicle credit (up to $4,000). Price cap $25,000; income limits $75k single/$150k joint. Terminated Sep 30, 2025 (OBBB).
Commercial clean vehicles: up to $7,500 (light) or $40,000 (heavy). No manufacturer cap; effective from 2023. Terminated Sep 30, 2025 (OBBB).
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit (amended)
Residential and commercial charging tax credits: up to $1,000 residential, up to $100,000 commercial. Terminated Jun 30, 2026 (OBBB).
Production tax credit for domestically produced battery cells, components, critical minerals. Battery cells: $35/kWh, modules: $10/kWh (or $45/kWh combined). Effective 2023, phase-down begins 2032.
Low-carbon hydrogen production credit (up to $3.00/kg H2), 4 tiers by carbon intensity. Supports hydrogen fuel cell vehicle development.
— IRA Critical Mineral & Battery Component Provisions
§30D Battery Component & Critical Mineral Sourcing Requirements

Phase-in: Critical minerals sourcing from US/FTA countries from 40% (2023) to 80% (2027); battery components from 50% (2023) to 100% (2029) N. America. FEOC prohibition: battery components from 2024, critical minerals from 2025.
IRS Issues Initial Clean Vehicle Credit Implementation Guidance
Published initial guidance for post-2022 clean vehicles, clarifying N. America assembly, income limits, MSRP caps; published list of qualifying vehicles.
Battery Component & Critical Mineral Requirements Take Effect
$7,500 credit split: $3,750 (critical minerals) × $3,750 (battery components). No credit if neither requirement met. First qualifying vehicle list released.
NHTSA Proposes CAFE Standards for MY 2027-2032
Proposed new passenger car and light truck CAFE standards (MY 2027-2032), targeting ~8% annual fuel efficiency improvement, working in tandem with EPA emissions standards.
IRA FEOC Final Rule (Non-Clean Vehicles Context)

Published definition and implementation rules for "Foreign Entity of Concern" — includes entities from/controlled by China, Russia, N. Korea, Iran. Battery component FEOC ban: 2024; critical minerals FEOC ban: 2025.
IRA §30D Critical Mineral Terms Final Rule
Finalized critical mineral definitions, qualifying sourcing calculations, and FTA country list (including S. Korea, Australia, etc.). ~50 minerals specified.
EPA Multi-Pollutant Emissions Standards for MY 2027-2032 (Final)
Requires ~56% reduction in GHG emissions from new passenger cars by 2032 vs 2026 standards. Most stringent tailpipe standards ever. EPA projected 67% EV market share by 2032.
Stringent GHG standards for commercial heavy-duty vehicles (MY 2027+), driving electric/hydrogen truck transition.
Formally published FEOC rules: from 2024, vehicles w/o FEOC battery components eligible for $3,750 component portion. FEOC mineral restriction effective 2025.
DOE Funds Battery & Critical Mineral Supply Chain Projects via IRA
Grants ($3.5B+) for domestic lithium processing, cathode/anode material production, battery recycling facilities.
NHTSA Final CAFE Standards for MY 2027-2032
Finalized MY 2027-2032 CAFE standards requiring ~2% (cars) / ~4% (light trucks) annual fuel efficiency improvement, reaching ~58 mpg equivalent by 2032.
Multiple states deploy NEVI-funded fast-charging stations (~every 50 miles on interstates). First sites operational in OH, NY, PA, others.
EO: Termination of Biden EV Mandate
Presidential EO directing all federal agencies to eliminate EV mandates and requirements. EPA directed to reconsider 2024 emissions standards.
Declared national energy emergency; revoked EV priority policies; rescinded multiple environmental EOs; expanded fossil fuel production.
EPA Reconsiders MY2027-2032 Standards & Heavy-Duty GHG Rule
Administrator Zeldin announces reconsideration of 2024 LD/MD multi-pollutant and HD GHG standards, claiming prior rules >$700B compliance costs.
EPA Launches Endangerment Finding Repeal Process
Initiated administrative process to repeal 2009 GHG Endangerment Finding — the legal foundation for all federal vehicle GHG regulations.
Federal EV Fleet Procurement Targets Canceled
Rescinded prior 5-year federal EV fleet procurement goals and preference policies; restores traditional vehicle procurement.
EPA Revokes CA ZEV Advanced Clean Cars Waiver
EPA revokes California's Clean Air Act waiver for voluntary ZEV push mechanism, limiting CA's ability to set stricter-than-federal standards. Finalized Nov 2025.
EPA CAFE Preemption Interim Final Rule
Published interim final rule prohibiting states from setting fuel economy standards independent of federal CAFE, directly targeting California's ACC and ZEV rules.
One, Big, Beautiful Bill (OBBB) — Major Tax Legislation

Signed as Public Law 119-21. Accelerated termination: §30D new EV credit (Sep 30, 2025), §25E used EV credit (Sep 30, 2025), §45W commercial EV credit (Sep 30, 2025), §30C charging credit (Jun 30, 2026).
IRS Issues OBBB Accelerated Termination FAQs
Clarifies "acquired" definition for EV credits under accelerated termination: entering binding contract + payment = acquired.

New clean vehicle ($7,500), used clean vehicle ($4,000), and commercial clean vehicle ($7,500-$40,000) credits stop accepting new applications. Previously contracted vehicles still eligible at delivery.
High tariffs imposed on Chinese imports including EV batteries & components, critical minerals. EV import tariffs raised to 100%+.
HJ Resolution: EPA Heavy-Duty NOx Standard Disapproval
CRA joint resolution to repeal 2022 EPA Heavy-Duty NOx emission standard.
CRA Resolution: EPA 2024 Light-Duty GHG Standards Disapproval
CRA joint resolution to repeal EPA 2024 Multi-Pollutant Standards (MY 2027-2032), signed by President. EPA directed to revert to 2020 SAFE rule levels.
[Needs verification] Proposed legislation under discussion to amend §45X production tax credit (battery components/critical minerals) terms and phase-down timeline.
NEVI Charging Infrastructure Fund Spending Tracker

[Status tracking, not a new policy] Status of the $7.5B NEVI federal fund disbursement and state-level charger deployment as of April 2026. Multiple states completed rounds of site awards, but overall spending slower than anticipated.

Per OBBB (Public Law 119-21), the federal charging infrastructure tax credit (§30C, up to $30,000/location) terminates Jun 30, 2026. This is the final step of OBBB clean energy tax repeal — §30D (new clean vehicle $7,500), §25E (used clean vehicle $4,000), §45W (commercial clean vehicle) had terminated Sep 30, 2025.
